Requirement Details Tendering Procedure: Selective Tendering This requirement is open only to those TBIPS Supply Arrangement Holders who qualified under Tier 1 for services in the National Capital Region for the following categories: • Category A.1. Application/Software Architect Level 3 • Category I.2. Database Administrator Level 3 • Category I.6. Network Analyst Level 3 • Category I.11. Technology Architect Level 3 The following SA Holders have been invited to submit a proposal: • Accenture Inc. • ADRM Technology Consulting Group Corp. • BoonBridge Corporation • CDW Canada Corp. • CGI Information Systems and Management Consultants Inc. • Cofomo Inc. • Deloitte Inc. • Donna Cona Inc., IBM Canada Limited Joint Venture • Flex Tech Services Inc • Primex Project Management Limited • Prologic Systems Ltd., and Maplesoft Consulting Inc. in JV • Skyfly Solutions Inc., iFathom Corp., EPI-Use Now Inc. in Joint Venture • Spaghetti Logic Inc. • TRM Technologies Inc. • Xelerance Corporation Description of Work: The objective of this requirement is to augment knowledge within the Department of Justice Canada’s (JUS) Cloud team to gather expertise and meet project requirements and specific AI initiatives. The required professional services will support the delivery of key infrastructure components, networking fixes and improvements as well as high visibility projects such as Otto , Artificial Intelligence and the Lakehouse. The Cloud Engineer will implement, configure, automate, and support cloud infrastructure, platform services, and cloud-native solutions in accordance with Government of Canada Cloud Guardrails, departmental standards, enterprise architecture principles, and security controls. The Cloud Engineer will support the deployment, integration, modernization, and operational management of Microsoft Azure services, enterprise applications, AI-enabled solutions, and hybrid cloud environments. The Cloud Engineer will collaborate with the Cloud Centre of Expertise (CCoE), Shared Services Canada (SSC), Security Operations, infrastructure teams, application teams, and project stakeholders to deploy, configure, monitor, troubleshoot, automate, and document cloud services, platform components, application hosting environments, identity services, storage, networking, and operational processes while supporting continuous improvement, operational excellence, and knowledge transfer. The Cloud Architect will design, document, and provide technical leadership for the Department's cloud architecture, ensuring compliance with Government of Canada Cloud Guardrails, departmental standards, security controls, and enterprise architecture principles. The Cloud Architect will support cloud infrastructure, cloud-native applications, application modernization initiatives, Azure platform services, AI-enabled solutions, and hybrid architectures. Responsibilities include the design of governance models, subscription hierarchies, landing zones, security architecture, integration patterns, DevSecOps practices, application hosting models, and reference architectures to support enterprise cloud adoption and integration with on-premises and cloud-based services. The Network Specialist will design, implement, document, and support cloud and hybrid networking solutions that provide secure, resilient, and high-performing connectivity between cloud, on-premises, partner, and externally hosted environments. The specialist will support enterprise cloud platforms, cloud-native applications, application modernization initiatives, AI-enabled solutions, and hybrid architectures by designing and implementing networking services, secure integration patterns, and connectivity solutions. The Network Specialist will collaborate with Shared Services Canada (SSC), internal Security Operations, infrastructure teams, application teams, and project stakeholders to design, implement, validate, and document network connectivity, firewall configurations, DNS services, certificate management, identity integration, private connectivity, and network security controls in accordance with Government of Canada standards and departmental policies. The Database Administrator will design, implement, maintain, and optimize database platforms across on-premises and Azure environments, ensuring the availability, performance, security, and recoverability of business-critical systems. The Database Administrator will implement and support backup, restore, high availability, disaster recovery, monitoring, and security controls, while providing technical advice and documentation related to database migrations, cloud integration, and operational best practices in coordination with application teams, Shared Services Canada (SSC), and internal security stakeholders. Bidders must submit a bid for all resource categories. Security Requirement: All Contractor personnel must hold at a minimum, a Personnel security screening level of Reliability. Privileged users require a Personnel Security screening level of Secret. Unscreened personnel are prohibited from performing services under the Contract. Minimum Corporate Security Required: Reliability Minimum Resource Security Required: Secret Contract Authority Name: Ryan Greig Phone Number: 437-295-5631 Email Address: Ryan.Greig@justice.gc.ca Inquiries Inquiries regarding this RFP requirement must be submitted to the Contracting Authority named above. Request for Proposal (RFP) documents will be e-mailed directly from the Contracting Authority to the Qualified Supply Arrangement Holders who are being invited to bid on this requirement. title: Reopening of the Over 65 Residential Care Home Framework for Swindon
description: Swindon Borough Council invites expressions of interest from suitably qualified and experienced service providers for admission to the existing Over 65 Years of Age Residential Care Home Framework for Swindon. Project Description Swindon Borough Council is undertaking the first annual re-opening of its existing Residential Care Home Framework for adults aged 65 years and over within the Swindon locality. This Framework was originally commissioned under public contract regulations and will continue to use this until the end of the total term. This framework commenced on 1st January 2026 and is currently operating within the initial contract period. Existing Framework providers are not required to reapply as part of this process. Successful applicants will join the existing Framework from 1st January 2027. This procurement exercise does not constitute a new procurement or re-tender of the Framework. It provides an opportunity for providers that are not currently admitted to the Framework, or that were unsuccessful in previous application rounds, to apply for admission to the Framework. The Framework has an initial term ending on 31st December 2027, with the option for the Council to extend by up to two further periods of two years each, resulting in a maximum potential Framework duration of six years from the original commencement date. Providers admitted through this re-opening exercise may remain on the Framework for the remainder of the Framework term, subject to extension options being exercised and continued compliance with contractual requirements. The estimated value of placements commissioned through the Framework during the period 1st January 2027 to 31st December 2027 is approximately £12 million, with a potential maximum Framework value of approximately £60 million should all extension periods be exercised. The Framework will continue to be re-opened annually via the Supplying the South West Portal to allow additional providers to apply for admission. The Framework will be advertised and all applicants must meet the minimum selection and award criteria to be admitted to the Framework. This Framework is for in-borough residential care homes only. For all over-65 residential care needs (standard, enhanced and complex), providers will be required to operate within the Council's published fee structure. Acceptance of the Council's fee structure will form part of the Framework requirements. To participate, suppliers must register as a supplier with ProContract at www.supplyingthesouthwest.org.uk and register an interest in the opportunity before obtaining access to the tender documents. In the event of difficulties registering as a supplier, please contact the Proactis Support Team at ProContractSuppliers@proactis.com Tender clarification deadline: 7th October 2026, 12:00 noon (UK Local Time). Clarification questions must be submitted via the Messaging facility within the ProContract portal. Responses will be issued periodically through the portal. Tender submission deadline: 14th October 2026, 12:00 noon (UK Local Time), via the ProContract portal: https://www.supplyingthesouthwest.org.uk/ Please note that this opportunity may be advertised on Find a Tender Service, Contracts Finder and other procurement websites; however, Supplying the South West Portal is the only portal containing all documentation required to submit a response. title: 2027 Southern Hemisphere Influenza Vaccine
description: The Defense Logistics Agency Troop Support is soliciting for the supply of Southern Hemisphere Influenza Vaccine for the 2027-2028 flu season. Approximately 30,000 doses are included in this requirement. (Quantities may increase or decrease pending receipt of final Service requirements.) The vaccines shall be a pre-measured 0.5 ML dose, each dose shall be pre-filled in a commercially available syringe for intramuscular administration in healthy individuals aged 6 months and older. The vaccine shall be U.S. Food & Drug Administration (FDA)-approved and U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) recommended. The formula for the 2027-2028 season vaccine shall be determined by the FDA�s Vaccines and Related Biological Products Advisory Committee. Other specification data is included in the solicitation. Successful contractor must have FDA Approval and the vaccine must be ACIP recommended. National Stock Numbers shall be established at time of award. An indefinite quantity contract is proposed. The quantity indicated is an annual estimate only. (Quantities may increase or decrease pending receipt of final Service requirements.) The guaranteed minimum will be 75% of the annual estimate, and a contract maximum will be established at 150% of the annual estimate. All quantities shall be delivered to the Defense Depot New Cumberland, PA. The contractor shall be capable of delivering 100% of the requirements by March 12, 2027. This delivery schedule is the preferred delivery schedule. Other delivery schedules will be considered. A copy of the solicitation will be posted to the DLA Bid Board System (DIBBS) at https://www.dibbs.bsm.dla.mil and SAM.gov at https://www.sam.gov. title: Finland – Translation services – Viittomakielisten tulkkausten ja käännösten hankinta valtioneuvostolle
description: Valtioneuvoston kanslia (VNK) on yksi 12 ministeriöstä. Sen päätehtävä on tukea pääministeriä valtioneuvoston johtamisessa sekä hallituksen ja eduskunnan työn yhteensovittamisessa. VNK vastaa valtioneuvoston toiminnan organisoinnista ja hallituksen toimintaedellytysten järjestämisestä kaikissa olosuhteissa. Hankinnan kohteena ovat valtioneuvoston ja sen ministeriöiden tarvitsemien suomalaisen ja suomenruotsalaisen viittomakielen tulkkaus- ja käännöspalveluiden hankinta. Tulkkaus- ja käännöspalveluita tarvitaan pääsääntöisesti suomesta ja/tai ruotsista suomalaiselle ja suomenruotsalaiselle viittomakielelle, mutta jonkin verran myös suomalaisesta ja suomenruotsalaisesta viittomakielestä suomeksi. Viittomakielisiä tulkkaus- ja käännöspalveluita tarvitaan erityisesti 1.7.2026 valtioneuvoston kansliassa aloittaneen valtioneuvoston viestintäosaston tarpeisiin. Valtioneuvoston viestintäosasto vastaa valtioneuvoston ja sen ministeriöiden viestinnästä ja valtionhallinnon viestinnän yhteensovittamisesta. Suositus viittomakielten käytöstä valtioneuvoston viestinnässä 2025 edistää viittomakielisten kielellisten oikeuksien toteutumista. Viestintään liittyvien tulkkaus- ja käännöspalveluiden lisäksi hankinnan kohteena ovat myös ministeriöiden muut viittomakieliset tulkkaus- ja käännöstarpeet (osa-alueet 5-8), joiden hankinnassa valtioneuvoston kanslia toimii hankintarenkaan vetäjänä ja hankintarenkaassa ovat mukana liikenne- ja viestintäministeriö, oikeusministeriö, opetus- ja kulttuuriministeriö, sosiaali- ja terveysministeriö, ulkoministeriö ja valtiovarainministeriö sekä oikeuskanslerinvirasto. Tulkkaukset ja käännökset voivat koskea mitä tahansa ministeriöiden toimialoihin kuuluvaa asiaa, ks. valtioneuvoston ohjesääntö 262/2003, § 10–24, https://www.finlex.fi/fi/laki/ajantasa/2003/20030262. Lisätietoa ministeriöiden toiminnasta on saatavilla ministeriöiden www-sivustoilla, ks. https://valtioneuvosto.fi/ministeriot Hankinta on EU-kynnysarvon ylittävä palveluhankinta ja se on jaettu kahdeksaan osa-alueeseen: 1. Tiedotustilaisuuksien tulkkaukset suomesta suomalaiselle viittomakielelle 2. Tiedotustilaisuuksien tulkkaukset suomesta ja ruotsista suomenruotsalaiselle viittomakielelle 3. Viestintään liittyvät käännökset suomesta suomalaiselle viittomakielelle 4. Viestintään liittyvät käännökset ruotsista suomenruotsalaiselle viittomakielelle 5. Muut tulkkaukset suomesta suomalaiselle viittomakielelle ja suomalaisesta viittomakielestä suomeksi 6. Muut tulkkaukset suomesta ja ruotsista suomenruotsalaiselle viittomakielelle ja suomenruotsalaisesta viittomakielestä suomeksi ja ruotsiksi 7. Muut käännökset suomesta suomalaiselle viittomakielelle 8. Muut käännökset ruotsista suomenruotsalaiselle viittomakielelle Tarjoaja voi tehdä tarjouksen yhdelle tai useammalle osa-alueelle. Kullekin osa-alueelle perustetaan puitejärjestely, jossa valitut toimittajat on asetettu etusijajärjestykseen. Hankinnan ennakoitu arvo on kaikki kielet yhteenlaskettuna noin 100 000 euroa/vuosi. Valittavien toimittajien kanssa tehdään kahden vuoden (24 kk) puitesopimus, joka sisältää kaksi yhden (1) vuoden optiota. Sopimuskauden arvioitu alkamisajankohta on 1.11.2026.

title: Revvity Electronic Laboratory Notebook FedRAMP Authorization
description: Based on the market research conducted, the Government proceeded with a fixed-price, sole-source acquisition with Revvity Signals Software, Inc. (Revvity) for the services necessary to obtain FedRAMP Moderate authorization for the Revvity Signals Electronic Lab Notebook (ELN), supporting compliance with NARA/OMB requirements for the transition of Federal records to electronic formats. The contractor is responsible for providing the services necessary to obtain FedRAMP Moderate authorization for the Revvity Signals ELN, including project management, gap remediation, interoperability assurance, and preparation and submission of the FedRAMP authorization package. Revvity is the developer and sole proprietary owner of the Revvity Signals ELN platform used by the National Institutes of Health (NIH). As the software owner, Revvity has exclusive access to the platform�s source code, system architecture, and internal development environment. Such access is necessary to perform the security control remediation, interoperability configuration, and technical documentation required to achieve FedRAMP Moderate authorization. No other company, including resellers, integrators, or third-party consultants, has the technical access or authority necessary to modify the Revvity platform to satisfy these requirements. On August 7, 2026, the Government posted a Notice of Intent and invited capability statements from vendors that believed they were capable of performing the work specified in the notice. Responses were due by 9:00 a.m. on August 14, 2026. Four vendors submitted timely responses; however, none demonstrated the technical capability necessary to perform the required services. Specifically, the respondents lacked the proprietary access and requisite authority to perform the necessary FedRAMP remediation activities on the Revvity platform, and none provided a viable approach for obtaining or otherwise addressing the required access and authority. Accordingly, the market research did not identify an alternative source capable of meeting the Government�s requirements, and the acquisition proceeded on a sole-source basis with Revvity.

description: Project Number: 86262Infantry Platoon Battle Course (IPBC) Fort Bragg, North Carolina. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Savannah District is issuing an Invitation for Bid (IFB) W912HN26BA005 for project number: 86262 Infantry Platoon Battle Course (IPBC) Fort Bragg, North Carolina. Type of Contract and NAICS: This Acquisition is solicited using FAR Part 14, Sealed Bid Procedures for one (1) Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 236220- Commercial and Industrial Building Construction, with size standard of $45M.Type of Set-Aside: This acquisition is being offered under Full and Open Competition using the NAICS code identified above. Construction Magnitude: In accordance with DFARS 236.204, the magnitude of this construction project is anticipated to be between $10M-$25M. Bid Due Date: 15 June 2026 - 11:00am EDT via PIEE. Site Visit: 27 May 2026 - 09:00am EDT. Period of Performance: The period of performance including all options is 720 Calendar Days after the issuance of the notice to proceed. Project scope: This requirement is for the construction of a standard Automated Infantry Platoon Battle Course (IPBC). Primary facilities include the IPBC, small arms range operations control area, control tower (small), operations/storage building, covered bleacher, covered mess, ammunition breakdown building, building information systems, and latrine pads. Post Construction Award Services (PCAS) will be provided. Cybersecurity Measures will be incorporated into this project. Sustainability/energy measures will be provided. Supporting facilities include electric service, site improvements, and information systems. Project files are Portable Document Format (PDF) files and can be viewed, navigated, or printed using Adobe Acrobat Reader. Contractors must register at the SAM website at https://sam.gov to download the solicitation for this project. If/when issued, Amendments will be posted to the above-referenced website for electronic downloading. This will be the only method of distributing amendments before closing; therefore, the Offerors must check the website periodically for any amendments to the solicitation. Registrations: System for Award Management (SAM)-Offerors shall maintain an active registration in the SAM database at https://sam.gov to be eligible for a Government contract award. If an Offeror is not actively and successfully registered in the SAM database at the time of award, the Government reserves the right to award to the next prospective Offeror. Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE): The only authorized transmission method for bids in response to the forthcoming solicitation is electronic via Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) Solicitation Module. No Other Transmission Method (E-mail, Facsimile, U.S. Postal Mail, Hand Carried, etc.) Will Be Accepted. Offerors must have an active Proposal Manager role in PIEE at https://piee.eb.mil/.Point of Contacts: For this acquisition, the contracting officer, Jason Scheil, whose e-mail address is Jeremiah.J.Scheil@usace.army.mil, and the Contract Specialist, Brandon Moore, whose e-mail address is brandon.p.moore@usace.army.mil. Amendment 0002 - The purpose of this amendment is to publish the CAD files and to extend the bid opening date. The link and passcode for the CAD files are in the amendment document. *Note: Files are only available for 7 days after the posting of this amendment on DoD safe. Amendment 0003 - The purpose of this amendment is to provide additional drawings and specifications.

title: Industry Day U.S. Merchant Marine Academy Campus Modernization
description: FALL FY27 INDUSTRY DAY U.S. Merchant Marine Academy Campus Modernization Industry Day Special Notice | Thursday, October 15, 2026 Event Overview The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), New York District, and the U.S. Merchant Marine Academy (USMMA) will host the Fall FY27 Industry Day from 11:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. Eastern Time on October 15, 2026. The hybrid event will bring industry, government, community organizations, and other interested attendees together with USMMA and USACE leadership for an updated view of the Campus Modernization Initiative, its strategic direction, and anticipated procurement activity. This event is open to the general public, and interested vendors. The FY27-FY28 forecast will emphasize the substantial heavy construction opportunities central to the modernization program while also addressing utility upgrades and complementary supporting and non-construction requirements. In-person participation is strongly encouraged. Prior registration is required for every attendee and closes at 12:00 p.m. Eastern Time on October 12, 2026. Event Information Event: USMMA Campus Modernization Fall FY27 Industry Day Date: Thursday, October 15, 2026 Event Time: 11:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. Eastern Time Check-In: Opens at 10:00 a.m.; in-person attendees should arrive no later than 10:45 a.m. to allow at least 15 minutes for networking before the program begins Location: U.S. Merchant Marine Academy, 300 Steamboat Road, Kings Point, NY 11024; enter through the main gate Format: Hybrid; in-person attendance is strongly encouraged. Registered virtual attendees will receive a Microsoft Teams link on October 13, 2026 Audience: All interested attendees age 16 or older (public attendees welcome) Registration Deadline: 12:00 p.m. Eastern Time, Monday, October 12, 2026 Theme: USACE Partnering with Industry and the Local Community Industry Day Highlights The Industry Day program will include the following: Welcome and Keynote Remarks: USACE leadership, USMMA Academy leadership, and invited guests will discuss the modernization program, acquisition approaches, and community impacts. Strategic Program Overview: A general USMMA overview and FY27-FY28 Campus Modernization update, including the strategic vision, updated waterfall chart, and local-government and community considerations. Heavy Construction Forecast: A focused review of the significant heavy construction opportunities expected to drive the modernization program. Specific project names, dollar ranges, and acquisition methods will be presented at the event rather than released in this notice. Supporting and Utility Requirements: Discussion of utility upgrades and complementary non-construction requirements that support successful delivery of the broader construction program. Executive Panel and Q&A: A moderator-led discussion with USMMA leadership, USACE program representatives, and USACE Contracting, including questions and topics submitted by industry. Doing Business with the Government: A practical session presented by the USACE Office of Small Business Programs. Campus Tour and Networking: A campus tour and opportunities to engage with program managers, technical staff, government representatives, community stakeholders, and industry peers. Advance Industry Questions: Industry partners may submit proposed questions or discussion topics for the executive panel to Zachery.A.Bernard@usace.army.mil no later than September 30, 2026. Registration and Access Information Registration is required for every attendee, regardless of affiliation or attendance method. Email the information below to Zachery.A.Bernard@usace.army.mil no later than 12:00 p.m. Eastern Time on Monday, October 12, 2026. Use the subject line "USMMA FY27 Industry Day Registration." One representative may register multiple attendees, but the required information must be provided separately for each person. Full legal name of each attendee Organization, company, or other affiliation, if applicable Individual email address and telephone number for each attendee Attendance method: in person or virtual Company website, if applicable Current capability statement for industry participants Virtual Attendance: A Microsoft Teams link will be emailed to registered virtual attendees on October 13, 2026. In-person attendance is strongly encouraged. Campus Access Requirements All in-person attendees must present a valid REAL ID-compliant credential or another form of government-issued photo identification acceptable to USMMA security and comply with all campus-entry instructions provided to registered attendees. Logistics and Parking Campus Entrance: Use the main gate at 300 Steamboat Road, Kings Point, NY 11024. Parking: Free attendee parking is available in Marvin Lot; overnight parking is not permitted. Arrival: Check-in opens at 10:00 a.m. Allow time to enter, park, and walk to the event location; arrive no later than 10:45 a.m. for networking. On-Site Directions: Follow posted signs and directions from USMMA security and event personnel. Updates, Changes, and Cancellations Any material change to the schedule, format, access procedures, or event status will be announced through an amendment to this SAM.gov notice and by email to registered attendees. Notice Status and Disclaimer This announcement is for informational and advance-planning purposes only and is not a solicitation or Government commitment to award a contract. The Government will not reimburse costs associated with this notice or event. Attendance is not required to participate in a future acquisition, and all event information is subject to change. Primary Point of Contact Name: Zachery A. Bernard Title: Deputy, Office of Small Business Programs (OSBP) Organization: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, North Atlantic Division - New York District Email: Zachery.A.Bernard@usace.army.mil Registration Email Subject: USMMA FY27 Industry Day Registration END OF SPECIAL NOTICE

title: Webhosting und fachliche Unterstützung (Expertisepool) für das „Qualitätssiegel Nachhaltiges Gebäude“ (QNG)
description: Auftraggeberin ist die PD Berater der Öffentlichen Hand GmbH. Eine Kundin der Auftraggeberin hat 2021 mit dem „Qualitätssiegel Nachhaltiges Gebäude“ (QNG) eine Dachmarke des nachhaltigen Bauens in Deutschland gegründet. Mit dem „Qualitätssiegel Nachhaltiges Gebäude“ (QNG) soll das nachhaltige Bauen in Deutschland in die Breite getragen werden und eine Mindestqualität für „nachhaltige Gebäude“ sichergestellt werden. Außerdem soll eine rechtssichere Grundlage für die Vergabe von Fördermitteln geschaffen werden, die Zuwendungen im Baubereich in Übereinstimmung mit gesellschaftlichen Zielen (Nachhaltigkeitszielen) ermöglicht. Seit 2022 unterstützt die Auftraggeberin die Kundin mit dem Aufbau und der Etablierung einer QNG Geschäftsstelle mit allen dazugehörigen Tätigkeiten, wie z.B. Hotline, Betrieb einer Website und Weiterentwicklung der QNG-Anforderungen mit den dazugehörigen Veröffentlichungen. Um aktuelle Informationen über das Siegel und den einzuhaltenden Prozessen zur Verfügung zu stellen, wurde im Jahr 2022 die QNG Website https://www.qng.info/ mit einem externen Dienstleister entwickelt und aufgebaut. Die QNG Website stellt eine Wissensplattform dar, die laufende Entwicklungen und Veränderungen aufarbeitet, grundsätzliche Abläufe, Schnittstellen sowie Hilfestelllungen den Nutzern bereit-stellt. Die Vergabe erfolgt in zwei Losen: - Los 1: Hosting, Weiterentwicklung und Betreuung der bestehenden Website - Los 2: Fachliche Unterstützung (Expertisepool) für das „Qualitätssiegel Nachhaltiges Gebäude“ (QNG). Die losspezifischen Aufgaben werden im Folgenden näher beschreiben. Geboten werden kann für ein oder für beide Lose.

Scope: The scope of the work is to provide a durable waterproofing system for the Dworshak powerhouse and ancillary roofs. This will be achieved by removing the existing roofing system in its entirety down to the structural roof decks, followed by the installation of a new fully adhered roofing assembly to include gypsum roof sheathing, a vapor retarder, polyisocyanurate foam roof insulation, cover board, and 90-mil EPDM membrane. A 2-year installer warranty and a 30-year manufacturer warranty are required. Fall protection guardrails constructed from fiber-reinforced plastic (FRP) will be installed to the parapet walls of the powerhouse and elevator penthouse roofs to ensure a safe work environment for maintenance personnel conducting preventative maintenance activities on the roofs. Fabricated metal stairs will be installed to replace existing ladder access to two roof areas. The mechanical air conditioning unit for the elevator machine room will be replaced with a new split heat pump system with indoor air handler and outdoor condenser unit. Roof parapet heights above the parking lot/roadway range from 36 feet high to 75 feet high. Cranes and/or telescopic boom lifts will be necessary to deliver material on to the roof surfaces. buyer: Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH
title: Germany – Vocational training services – 10018858-Implementation of TVET support and women's economic empowerment activities in Sierra Leone
description: Sierra Leone faces persistent poverty, high informality and limited job creation, disproportionately affecting women and youth. Agriculture is the largest employer, yet value chains are fragmented, processing is weak, and access to finance, quality infrastructure and certification is limited. The Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) system suffers from outdated curricula, insufficient equipment and low private sector engagement, constraining labour market relevance, especially for women and returnees. The "Youth Employment Promotion through Socio Ecological and Economic Transformation of selected rural Value Chains" (EET project), commissioned by BMZ with EU co funding, supports inclusive, market oriented growth and better employment along selected value chains (cassava, coffee/cocoa, vegetables, poultry). It strengthens micro, small and medium sized enterprises (MSMEs) and the enabling ecosystem, with a strong focus on Women's Economic Empowerment (WEE) and youth integration. The project applies a concise multi level approach: support MSMEs with training, coaching and finance to improve productivity and market access; strengthen ecosystem actors (finance, certification, cooperatives, processing centres) to enhance services and linkages; and upgrade TVET through demand driven Competence Based Education and Training (CBET) curricula, improved facilities at Government Technical Institutes (GTIs) in Kabala, Kailahun, Koidu and Mattru Jong, teacher capacity building and institutionalised private sector engagement for apprenticeships and certification via Industry Sector Advisory Committees. WEE is embedded throughout. The project strengthens six representative bodies advancing women's economic rights (e.g. Gender Equality and Women's Empowerment - GEWE - Act), introduces gender transformative modules (Gender makes Business Sense - GmBS; Gender Action Learning Systems - GALS; Gender Model Family - GMF) via public and private providers, and delivers mentoring and awareness campaigns to address norms and improve women"s access to resources, markets and decision making. Outcomes are tracked with recognised tools such as the (pro )Women's Empowerment in Agriculture Index (pro WEAI). Key results targeted include: - Improved competitiveness of MSMEs with measurable employment effects for women and youth. - Upgraded GTIs and at least nine demand oriented, gender responsive curricula operational; teachers trained in learner centred CBET; trainees certified in line with National Council for Technical and Vocational Education (NCTVE) standards in the initial phase. - Stronger institutional conditions for women's economic participation, including operational representative bodies, integrated gender transformative modules, and functioning mentoring and communication platforms. - Enhanced market access through strengthened outgrower networks, cooperative services and business linkages, enabling more equitable participation of women and young producers. The approach is rights based, conflict and context sensitive, and climate aware. It promotes green and circular economy elements in training and enterprise support, limits environmental footprints and applies Do No Harm principles. Implementation aligns with national policies (TVET Policy, Dual Apprenticeship Policy) under the coordination of the Ministry of Planning and Economic Development, with the Ministry of Technical and Higher Education (MTHE) and NCTVE responsible for TVET standards and certification, and the Ministry of Gender and Children's Affairs and civil society partners advancing WEE. Continuous monitoring, learning and adaptive management ensure data driven steering and accountability to BMZ and the EU. EU visibility will follow EU visual identity guidelines; co branding with BMZ/GIZ will follow donor rules.?

buyer: HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES, DEPARTMENT OF
title: JOFOC for Data Analysis for Quality, Safety & Oversight of the ESRD, Transplant, and OPO Programs
description: The contractor will provide detailed data reports about End Stage Renal Disease (ESRD) facilities (commonly referred to as dialysis facilities), Transplant Programs, and Organ Procurement Organizations (OPOs) in formats that are useful to the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), states, health care providers, and the general public. These reports will include summaries of patient characteristics, facility characteristics, patient outcomes, and facility practice patterns. These reports will include comparative state, network, regional, and national statistics as appropriate. These reports will be used by CMS in overseeing the quality and safety of the ESRD, Transplant and OPO Programs. For the Dialysis Facility Reports (DFRs), the contractor will use data from a variety of sources to create summary reports to be used to provide Federal, state and facility oversight of dialysis facilities. Data from all available sources, including the CMS Central Data Repository (CDR), claims forms, eligibility forms, clinical data sources, facility inventories, death forms, and survey and certification forms will be updated, edited, validated, and utilized by the contractor to create a series of reports that will assist CMS, states, and other entities in monitoring the care provided by ESRD facilities. These reports will be risk-adjusted and facility, state, regional, and corporate-specific for each fiscal year. The reports shall include a rank-ordered Outcomes List of ESRD facilities for each state. The Outcomes Lists will be constructed from a composite of data elements that most validly and reliably identify facilities with potential problems. The contractor will routinely revise the DFRs to ensure they are 1) aligned with the ESRD Survey process, 2) provide development of data sources and data tools to allow state surveyors convenient and timely access to more current dialysis facility quality outcomes, 3) use state surveyor and other DFR user feedback to determine the need for revisions. The contractor will provide guidance on using advanced technologies and incorporate plans to integrate emerging technologies associated with Electronic Health Records (EHRs). The contractor will prepare Transplant Program reports and OPO reports. The data for these reports will be obtained from the Scientific Registry of Transplant Recipients (SRTR) of the Health Resources and Services Agency (HRSA), the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), and Multiple Cause of Death (MCOD) databases. This data will be used in the calculation of annual OPO performance measure scores as required by the CMS regulations at 42 CFR �486.318.

title: Government of Canada Building HVAC Replacement – Calgary, Alberta
description: The Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) intends to retain a contractor to provide construction services for the replacement of an HVAC system and associated equipment that have reached the end of their useful life. The building, located in Calgary, Alberta, was constructed in 1986 and is approximately 1,547 m² in size (930 m² on the main floor and 617 m² in the basement). The scope of work includes, but is not limited to, the removal and replacement of existing heating and air conditioning equipment, an air handling unit, make-up air unit, pumps and recirculation pumps, sump pump, and hot water tank. The project also includes the rerouting of ductwork, wiring, devices, and insulation; the relocation and upgrade of the Building Management System (BMS); and associated electrical and control work. Additional work includes targeted partition demolition, refrigerant-related work, installation of chain-link fencing, vents, grilles and louvers, thermostats, testing and balancing, setpoint optimization, and commissioning. The contract period will be until March 31, 2027 This solicitation of bids is open only to Canadian suppliers. There will be a Phase Two site visit. The date, time and location for the Phase Two site visit will be identified during Phase Two to the responsive Phase one bidders. title: AC/MC-130J Arkham SMP Production
description: Arkham Special Mission Processor (SMP): The Government is conducting market research to identify potential sources that possess the expertise, capabilities, facilities, and experience to manufacture, assemble, test, and deliver a total of 94 Arkham SMP Production Kits and 55 Spares. The Arkham SMP is a mission processor utilizing Sensor Open System Architecture (SOSA) in support of AC/MC-130J system integration. The Arkham SMP is separated into two (2) major processing areas: Video Processing/General Processing and Safety Critical Processing. The Video Processing/General Processing is done on five (5) Intel based General Purpose Processor Modules. The Safety Critical Processing is done on two (2) ARM based Safety Critical Processor (SCP) modules. The network includes a red and an internal NextGen SMP gold (same classified level with different subnets), and two unclassified black for multiple levels of security. Safety Critical Processing is separated into Red/Gold and Black zones. The Arkham SMP must utilize LYNXOS and Red Hat Enterprise Linux as the operating system. The acquisition strategy is for the contractor to provide kit production with a period of performance of seven (7) Years. The kit will include the following: Two (2) Arkham Units, two (2) External Data Storage (EDS) Devices, two (2) one (1) TB Delkin Solid State Drives (SSD), and other hardware required for aircraft installation. This will provide the AC/MC-130J mission with enhanced abilities for search and rescue in increased threat environments. Potential Sources must be capable of developing prototype hardware, software, and all associated technical data necessary to be able to produce and deliver the Arkham Production Kit and Spares. The Potential Source must be able to fully test and evaluate the function and performance of the Arkham Production Kit and Spares. The Potential Source must be capable of developing and providing the source data necessary to update AFTO�s and TDPs.

description: Amendment W519TC26RA0360001 Please use the following link to access Amendment W519TC26RA0360001: https://piee.eb.mil/sol/xhtml/unauth/search/oppMgmtLink.xhtml?noticeId=W519TC26RA036&noticeType=SolicitationNotice NOTE: The Government is utilizing the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) website to release the RFP/Solicitation and to receive proposals for the subject procurement. The PIEE website communicates with SAM.gov, however, there is a technical issue that is preventing the PIEE announcement of the subject RFP/Solicitation release from reaching SAM.gov. There is a chance there will be a duplication of this announcement in SAM.gov in the future; however, the PIEE link above will remain valid. _________________________________________________________________________ General Information The Army Contracting Command - Rock Island Arsenal (ACC-RIA) and the U.S. Army, Product Lead Special Ammunition and Weapon Systems (PdL SAWS) herein issues Solicitation W519TC26RA036. This is for the procurement of Special Ammunition and Weapon Systems (SAWS) and non-North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) standard ammunition. This is in support of the Department of War (DoW), other U.S. Government (USG) Agencies, foreign governments, and international organizations. This requirement requires highly capable Prime Contractors to procure and deliver a diverse portfolio of Non-Standard Ammunition (NSA) and select Non-Standard Weapon Systems (NSWS). The primary objective of this program is to establish reliable, agile, and responsive supply chains capable of sourcing specialized, foreign produced munitions and weapons systems. These materiel requirements support the National Security Strategy and enable the National Military Strategy for joint warfighters, USG agencies, and international allies or coalition partners. The USG is seeking partners who can guarantee quality and safety despite the "non-standard" nature of these weapons. While these items are not type-classified for U.S. troop use, the Contractor will be strictly evaluated on its ability to provide experience of implementing rigorous quality control, visual and physical inspections, and ballistic testing to deliver safe, reliable, and effective SAWS. The applicable North Atlantic Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition is 332993 - Ammunition (except Small Arms) Manufacturing Procurement Categories The ammunition and weapon systems to be procured fall within the following Federal Supply Groups (FSGs) provided in the SAWS Tailored Federal Supply Classification (FSC) Item List (Attachment 0001). With limited exceptions, all items must be compatible with the applicable weapons within their associated General Specification(s) for PdL SAWS (Attachments 0003 - 0007). FSGs and subordinate FSC codes used as a basis for categories (Attachment 0001). Contract and Award Details Source Selection A Highest Technically Rated Offeror (HTRO) source selection approach will be utilized. This is referenced in the DoD Source Selection Procedures (para 1.3.1.5) and will be conducted in accordance with Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) 15.103-3 and the DoD Source Selection Procedures. Technical Experience Evaluation Offerors are required to use the HTRO Self-Score Matrix (Attachment 0008) to self-score their past technical experience. To substantiate their self-scores, Offerors must submit work samples documenting relevant past technical experience as either a Prime Contractor or a Subcontractor. title: Sovereign Cloud Invitation to Qualify
description: NATIONAL SECURITY EXCEPTION In respect of all phases of the solicitation, SSC has invoked the National Security Exception (NSE). As such, this invocation exempts all phases of the procurement processes for sovereign cloud services from the application of all of Canada’s trade agreements, including the World Trade Organization Agreement on Government Procurement (Article III(1)) and the Canadian Free Trade Agreement (Article 801). 1. INTRODUCTION The Government of Canada (GC) is advancing its digital infrastructure and hosting capabilities to meet evolving operational requirements and to deliver services to Canadians that are secure, reliable, and user-centric. Building on findings and industry feedback obtained through prior engagement activities, Shared Services Canada (SSC) is establishing a structured Sovereign Cloud Qualification Process as an initial step to support future procurements. The Sovereign Cloud Qualification process is intended to: • Establish a standing entry point for Canadian-owned and -controlled businesses seeking to qualify to participate in sovereign cloud procurements • Enable Canada to collect information on available and emerging offerings to support market awareness and procurement planning • Provide a consistent, transparent, and accessible mechanism for industry engagement • This Notice of Planned Procurement does not constitute a commitment by Canada to issue any solicitation or to procure any services. 2. PROCESS OVERVIEW The Sovereign Cloud Qualification Process is supported by an Invitation to Qualify (ITQ). The ITQ defines the requirements for qualification, including: • Eligibility conditions • Submission requirements • Supporting documentation • Process instructions The qualification process serves as the entry point and a mandatory step for vendors to participate in current and future sovereign cloud procurement processes. Vendors that participate in the qualification process and meet the eligibility conditions defined in the ITQ will be considered as Qualified Respondents (QR) for participation in future sovereign cloud procurement opportunities. This qualification process is not a competitive procurement process and will not result in a contract award. It is intended solely to establish a list of qualified vendors for participation in future procurement activities. 3. ELIGIBILITY CONDITIONS Eligibility conditions details are defined in the ITQ (available in tab “Bidding Details” above). At a minimum, eligibility conditions include: - Confirmation of Respondent’s Canadian ownership and control, including parent companies. - Submission of a Value Proposition describing the respondent’s sovereign cloud offerings. 4. OBJECTIVE AND SCOPE 4.1 Objective The objective of the Sovereign Cloud Services procurement stream is to strengthen Canada’s cloud posture by enabling and supporting solutions that advance Canadian control over data and services, and protection from foreign legal or extraterritorial authority. The sovereign cloud procurement stream is intended to complement, and not replace, existing cloud procurement approaches. 4.2 Scope (Indicative Only) The service categories described below are indicative only and provided to inform respondents of the types of capabilities Canada may consider procuring in the future. Additional requirements, eligibility conditions, certifications, or evaluation criteria will be defined in future procurement stages once the procurement process is confirmed The scope of the Sovereign Cloud Services procurement stream may include, but is not limited to: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS): This category may include sovereign fundamental computing resources such as processing, storage, and networking. These services allow departments to deploy and run their own software, including operating systems and applications. While the cloud provider manages the underlying infrastructure, Canada retains control over operating systems, storage, deployed applications, and certain network configuration. Platform as a Service (PaaS): This category may include sovereign cloud services that allow departments to deploy and run applications built using programming languages, libraries, services, and tools supported by the provider. The provider manages the underlying infrastructure, including networks, servers, operating systems, and storage, while Canada retains control over the applications it deploys and the configuration of the application hosting environment. AI enabling services: This category may include sovereign services that support the development, deployment, or operation of artificial intelligence solutions, such as machine learning platforms, model hosting, data processing environments, and AI infrastructure. Managed Service Providers of Classified Cloud Solutions: This category may include managed services for classified cloud solutions. Vendors intending to operate as infrastructure providers will be required to provide certification from a recognized classified cloud solution provider in the Five Eyes confirming their authorization and agreement to deliver classified cloud services and associated managed solutions. Recognizing that many classified and unclassified cloud solutions are operated or owned by foreign providers, Canada may also consider managed service providers that have unique access to such cloud service solutions, even where those solutions are owned by foreign entities. In such cases, the managed service provider will need to demonstrate full control over the technology and the delivery of services. Other cloud or cloud enabling capabilities that support sovereign digital service delivery. This category may include other sovereign cloud or cloud-enabling capabilities not otherwise described in the indicative scopes provided above. 5. SUBMISSION PROCEDURES To participate in the Sovereign Cloud Qualification process, respondents must complete and submit the designated submission form in accordance with the requirements set out in the ITQ. 6. PROCESS AND TIMELINES The Sovereign Cloud Qualification process is open, ongoing, and continuously available through CanadaBuys. The ITQ defines intake periods and closing dates. The first intake period closing date is set to October 19, 2026. Following the end of each intake period, or more often at SSC’s discretion, responses will be assessed and each Respondent will be notified of its qualification status within 20 working days. SSC reserves the right to update, amend, or discontinue the Sovereign Cloud Qualification process at any time. 7. INFORMATION WEBINAR Vendors are invited to attend an Informational Webinar to discuss any questions you may have on the ITQ. Interested vendors must register by contacting the Contracting Authority before October 6, 2026, 23:59 Pacific Time, at the following email address: PVRCloudServicesRCRs.DCCServicesinfonuagiquesARF@ssc-spc.gc.ca. The Information Webinars will be held on the following dates and times: The French-language webinar will be held on October 8, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. – 11:00 a.m. EDT The English-language webinar will be held on October 8, 2026, at 1:00 p.m. – 2:00 p.m. EDT 8. FUTURE COMMUNICATION Vendors are responsible for monitoring CanadaBuys for updates related to this Sovereign Cloud Qualification. SSC may communicate updates or request clarification from respondents as required. 9. PRIVACY STATEMENT All responses will be treated as confidential, subject to the Access to Information Act and the Privacy Act. 10. TRADE AGREEMENTS No trade agreement applies to this requirement, as the National Security Exception has been invoked. 11. LANGUAGE Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada. 12. ENQUIRIES Enquiries regarding the Sovereign Cloud Qualification Process are to be submitted to: PVRCloudServicesRCRs.DCCServicesinfonuagiquesARF@ssc-spc.gc.ca

Nature of Requirements: The following is a summary of the statement of work for this requirement. The Correctional Service Canada has a requirement to replace the existing cell window glazing and installation of the polycarbonate security screens to prevent inmates from manipulating window assemblies and receiving contraband delivered by drone. Objectives: To improve the integrity and security of cell windows by installing enhanced glazing and security measures that prevent inmates from damaging, manipulating, removing, or otherwise compromising window assemblies to receive contraband. Deliverables: The Contractor shall: • Supply and install new security glazing in 168 windows located within POD 1 and POD 2, for a total of 504 glazing panels. • Supply and install one polycarbonate security screen on each of the 168 windows in accordance with the construction drawings. • Supply and install all required security screws, fasteners, and accessories identified in the construction drawings and specifications. • Apply security caulking to all newly installed glazing assemblies. • Apply security caulking to the 12 existing windows located in L-Range, POD 1. • Ensure all work is completed in accordance with the construction drawings, specifications, manufacturer’s instructions, and institutional security requirements. title: Low Profile Mast and Rotational Module Component Prototype Other Transaction Area of Interest
description: *9.23.2026: Updated Attachment 1: TOU to correct the listed PCO within the document. Team Submarines, Australia, United Kingdom, and United States (AUKUS), International & Systems (AI&S), Submarine Electromagnetic Systems Program Office (PMS 435) is pleased to release a competitive Area of Interest (AOI) announcement for the Low Profile Mast (LPM) and Rotational Module (RM) component to address several key operational needs. The LPM/RM programs seek innovative technologies that accelerate the prototyping of capabilities that address these key operational needs. To accelerate the design, development and demonstration of LPM/RM capabilities, the Navy will be utilizing the Other Transaction Authority pathway outlined in Title 10 U.S.C. � 4022. It is intended that this solicitation may result in the award of one or more prototype projects. There are nine (9) attachments to this AOI, some of which contain Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI): LPM/RM Terms of Use Agreement AOI AOI Guidance CUI LPM Type 24 Mod 1Top-Level Requirements Document [RESTRICTED] CUI LPM Verification Guide (VG) [RESTRICTED] CUI RM Top-Level Requirements Document [RESTRICTED] CUI RM Verification Guide [RESTRICTED] LPM/RM AOI Questions Form CUI LPM/RM Placemat Template [RESTRICTED] Companies are advised to proceed with the following steps to respond to this notice: STEP 1 � Terms of Use Agreement (TOU) Several key documents related to the LPM Type 24 Mod 1 and RM are only releasable to eligible businesses with ownership in the United States, the United Kingdom, and Australia. Non-Australia, United Kingdom, or United States foreign-owned businesses may submit a technical solution as part of a teaming arrangement with one or more Australia, United Kingdom, or United States-owned businesses. The ability to be awarded an Agreement may depend upon the ability of the Foreign-owned business to obtain necessary clearances and approvals to obtain access to restricted information. Companies interested in submitting a technical solution in response to the AOI shall complete Attachment 1: TOU Agreement and return it via e-mail to the Agreements Officer and Agreements Specialists listed in this notice. The Company point of contact that will request access to the restricted documents in this notice shall be the Company point of contact listed in the TOU. Companies should also request access to the restricted CUI documents in SAM at the time of TOU submittal to the Government. Once the signed TOU is received and verified, Team Submarines will grant access to the restricted CUI documents and transmit relevant UNCLASSIFIED Government-Furnished Information (GFI) to the Company point of contact listed in the TOU. NOTE: The TOU provided as Attachment 1 is specific to this AOI release; if a Company previously submitted a TOU under prior LPM/RM Industry Day notice, that Company must submit a separate TOU for this AOI opportunity. STEP 2 � QUESTIONS & ANSWERS OPPORTUNITY Companies may submit questions using Attachment 8: LPM/RM AOI Questions Form. Team Submarine will only accept Q&A submissions up to the CUI level. Q&A submissions shall be submitted electronically via e-mail to the Government points of contact listed in this notice no later than 6:00 p.m. Eastern Time on October 2, 2026. -SUBJECT: N00024-26-R-6215 Q&A This opportunity is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government, nor will the Government reimburse respondents for any questions submitted or for the information provided in response to this notice. The Government may or may not respond to Q&A submissions and reserves the right to redact the content of submissions prior to any release back to industry. The Government may use the information and feedback provided in Q&A submissions to inform future solicitations as necessary. Respondents are solely responsible for properly marking and clearly identifying any proprietary information or trade secrets contained in any submission in response to this notice. Opting not to submit any Q&A does not preclude participation in this AOI or any future engagements. It is the responsibility of industry to monitor the Government Point of Entry (GPE) for official AOI communications. STEP 4 - Companies shall submit Phase I White Papers and Placemats electronically via encrypted DoD SAFE transmission. Companies must request a DoD SAFE link by e-mailing ALL Government points contract listed in this notice no later than 6:00 p.m. Eastern Time on October 13, 2026. -SUBJECT: [insert LPM or RM] N00024-26-R-6215 DoD SAFE Link [insert COMPANY NAME] If a Company intends to send a Phase I submission for both LPM and RM, that Company must request two separate DoD SAFE links. Companies are encouraged to submit White Papers prior to the latest closing date. Inclusion of a delivery receipt with an email submission will be the only indication of the Government�s successful receipt of a White Paper. Each Company must comply with DoD SAFE file size limitations and other guidance as provided at https://safe.apps.mil/. Phase I submissions must be received by the Government via encrypted DoD SAFE submission no later than 6:00 p.m. Eastern Time on October 20, 2026. HARD COPIES OF MAILED OR HAND DELIVERED WHITE PAPERS WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED. Submissions sent through other channels not identified in this Notice, or after the Phase I White Paper submission deadline, will not be reviewed nor evaluated by the Government. title: Rental of Secure Storage Facility for ICE/ERO/Buffalo Field Office
description: The U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), Enforcement and Removal Operations (ERO) Buffalo Field Office requires secure storage for its Special Response Team (SRT) assets. These assets are currently held at the secure storage facility operated by the Town of Lancaster, NY at the Lancaster Police Department (LPD) facility located at 525 Pavement Road in Lancaster, NY. Approximately $500,000.00 of agency assets are stored at this facility. Storing these agency assets at any other secure storage facility in the Buffalo, NY metro area would present a significant logistical challenge with respect to the coordination of the pick-up/drop-off of assets at the two ICE/ERO facilities (Buffalo Field Office in downtown Buffalo and the Buffalo Federal Detention Facility (BFDF) in Batavia, NY) located within the ICE/ERO Buffalo Area of Responsibility (AoR) . It is therefore necessary to continue to utilize the LPD secure facility to store all SRT assets in a central location between the ICE/ERO Buffalo and Batavia facilities. The LPD facility is within close proximity (five miles) of the Buffalo-Niagara International Airport. Proximity to the airport is required because of the many times SRT is deployed to assist ERO flights at the airport. Based upon the Market Research conducted by ICE/ERO/Buffalo Field Office, and a consideration of available commercial sources and law enforcement organizations within 10 minutes (or around 5 miles) of the Buffalo-Niagara International Airport, the Contracting Officer has determined the Lancaster Police Department (LPD) is the only source that can meet the specifications stated in the Statement of Work (SOW) to provide secure storage for ICE/ERO/Buffalo Field Office SRT assets.

title: 6515--MC | VISN 15 Path & Lab | NEW ANATOMIC PATHOLOGY WORKFLOW | Base plus 4 | (VA-27-00002252) GS-07F-139CA
description: STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) Anatomic Pathology Specimen Tracking System VISN 15 Pathology and Laboratory Services 1.0 General 1.1 The Contractor shall provide and configure an Anatomic Pathology (AP) Specimen Tracking System to support end to end tracking of AP specimens, cassettes, and slides from accessioning through final disposition in alignment with the Federal EHR Baseline and Oracle Health Commercial Model. 1.2 The solution shall fully support high volume AP laboratory operations, including complex workflows and telepathology/digital pathology use cases. 1.3 The AP Specimen Tracking System shall have pre existing Oracle Health CareAware device drivers and pre existing integration with Oracle Health Advanced Barcoding and Tracking (AB&T); custom development of CareAware drivers or AB&T integration for the proposed product is out of scope for this effort. 1.4 The proposed AP Specimen Tracking System shall demonstrate a production implementation of CareAware and AB&T integration with Oracle Health in a hospital AP environment. 1.5 The system shall support barcode driven workflows to reduce manual data entry, minimize typographical errors, and improve patient safety, including support for multiple patient identifiers on blocks and slides consistent with applicable VA/VHA policy. 2.0 Scope 2.1 The AP Specimen Tracking System shall be utilized for all Anatomic Pathology and Cytology specimens within the Pathology and Laboratory Services at the following sites: St. Louis Pathology and Laboratory Services Kansas City Pathology and Laboratory Services Marion Pathology and Laboratory Services The Contractor shall provide services and support at the locations identified in this Statement of Work. The Government reserves the right to add, remove, or modify locations and facilities as mission requirements evolve across the current and future operational footprint. The Contractor shall accommodate these changes within the scope of the contract without disruption to services. Any adjustments to pricing, schedule, or resources resulting from such changes shall be addressed through the appropriate contractual modification process in accordance with the applicable Changes clause. 2.2 The system shall support workflow at a minimum for accessioning, specimen receipt, grossing, embedding, microtomy, staining, slide distribution, sign out, archival, and pathologist workstations at each of the sites listed in Section 2.1. At the pathologist workstation, the system shall support pathologist review of digital and/or physical slide information and shall enable the pathologist to originate orders for additional stains and recuts as part of the sign out workflow. 2.3 The Contractor shall provide all necessary software and hardware (including required drivers) to support connectivity with the VA Federal EHR environment and related AP instruments, in accordance with Federal EHR Baseline and Oracle Health guidance, for all sites listed in Section 2.1. 2.4 The Contractor shall provide any ancillary components (for example, barcode scanners, label printers, workstations, and interfaces) required for the AP Specimen Tracking System to function as specified at each site. 2.5 Site specific details such as floor plans, existing equipment inventories, and local interface diagrams are provided in Attachment A. 3.0 Applicable Documents 3.1 The Contractor shall perform all work in accordance with the most current versions of, but not limited to, the following as applicable: Federal EHR Baseline guidance for Anatomic Pathology and AP specimen tracking. Oracle Health Model and configuration guidance for AP components (including PathNet and AP Clinician Summary MPage). VA/VHA directives and handbooks related to patient identification, barcoding, and laboratory operations (e.g., two patient identifier requirements). VA Technical Reference Model (TRM) and Enterprise Risk Assessment (ERAR) requirements for software solutions. 4.0 Integration and Workflow Requirements 4.1 The Contractor shall integrate the AP Specimen Tracking System with the VA Federal EHR using existing Oracle Health CareAware and AB&T capabilities to enable barcode driven workflows for specimen receipt, grossing, embedding, microtomy, staining, slide distribution, and archival at St. Louis, Kansas City, and Marion Pathology and Laboratory Services. 4.2 The solution shall support automated printing and association of barcode labels for containers, cassettes, and slides in accordance with Federal EHR Baseline standards at each site. 4.3 The Contractor shall ensure that workflows configured in the AP Specimen Tracking System are compatible with Oracle Health AP components (for example, PathNet and AP Clinician Summary MPage) and adhere to Model compatible configuration patterns identified by Oracle Health. 4.4 For any of the sites that do not yet implement an AP Specimen Tracking System, the Contractor shall support manual AB&T usage via the AP Clinician Summary MPage with manually operated cassette and slide printers, consistent with Baseline guidance. 4.5 The system shall support configuration of barcode and label formats to enable interoperability with in house and third party AP instruments (for example, immunohistochemistry stainers, special stainers, cytology equipment, and slide imagers), without requiring custom software development. 4.6 Site specific interface endpoints, network details, and instrument connectivity requirements are further described in Attachment A. 5.0 Leica Cerebro as Exemplar Solution 5.1 An AP Specimen Tracking System of the type represented by Leica Cerebro is recognized within the Federal EHR Baseline as a solution that possesses pre existing CareAware drivers and AB&T integration and satisfies the Baseline standard for AP specimen tracking integration. 5.2 Baseline recommends that such a deployment serve as the first AB&T/CareAware/specialty vendor implementation and the model for subsequent AP specimen tracking deployments across VA. 5.3 Leica Cerebro is identified as an approved exemplar AP Specimen Tracking System for the purposes of this requirement; offerors may propose Leica Cerebro or an equivalent AP Specimen Tracking System that meets or exceeds all technical and integration requirements specified in Sections 1.0 and 4.0. 5.4 Any proposed alternative to Leica Cerebro shall provide documented evidence of existing Oracle Health CareAware drivers and AB&T integration and shall be capable of supporting national standardization of configuration and content as directed by VA Baseline governance. 6.0 National Standardization and Configurability 6.1 The Contractor shall support VA efforts to develop and enforce national standards for AP Specimen Tracking Systems, including a single national configuration, national technical integration points, and standardized clinical and business content across St. Louis, Kansas City, and Marion Pathology and Laboratory Services. 6.2 The AP Specimen Tracking System shall be configurable to align with these national standards, including the ability to adjust workflows, label formats, and integration parameters without custom code changes. 6.3 The Contractor shall participate, as requested, in VA National Standardization Projects related to AP tracking and digital pathology, providing technical information, configuration support, and test environments necessary to validate a single, reusable interface pattern for the approved AP Specimen Tracking System. 6.4 The Contractor shall ensure that AP tracking configuration and integration can be replicated consistently across VA sites, including St. Louis, Kansas City, and Marion Pathology and Laboratory Services, in accordance with Federal EHR Baseline governance. 7.0 Performance Requirements 7.1 The system shall support high volume AP operations (e.g., hundreds of tissue blocks and slides per day) with performance adequate to avoid workflow bottlenecks and delays in diagnosis at each site. 7.2
